segments.title: Setting up the recorder at Lee Friedlander's apartment
segments.summary: Recording test at Apartment 4G, Central Park West, on June 18, 1959; Danny Barker is surprised to see his grandfather's picture in the collection.

segments.title: George Lewis's mother, Alice Zeno and Edmund Hall's brother
segments.summary: They look at photos of George Lewis's mother, Alice Zeno, and a man identified as Edmund Hall's brother.

segments.title: Kid Thomas photo and the musician who plays two horns at once
segments.summary: Barker never worked with Kid Thomas; the photo shows his studio, his pupil and pictures of him playing two instruments at once, which Friedlander recalls hearing.

segments.title: Cook and Copperwire, notorious women of the district
segments.summary: Friedlander describes two rough women of the red-light district who were buddies; one is now blind and sick, and he talks about her time in Charity Hospital.

segments.title: Band photo, sidemen and the church of Mama Lou Washington
segments.summary: They try to name the players in a band photo with Celestin, then recall Mama Lou Washington's church and John Handy's mother.

segments.title: Sweet Emma's bells, Edmond Washington, Kid Poncho and a healer's card
segments.summary: They identify Emma, Edmond Washington who played with Kid Thomas, Kid Poncho, a healer's handbill, and Tats Alexander with Joe James.

segments.title: Veined hands, Piku and Tony, and a photo of Snooks Eaglin
segments.summary: Remarks on a man's veins, a failed attempt to place Tony, and an introduction to a photo of Snooks Eaglin.

segments.title: Stopping the machine until later
segments.summary: Barker must leave around nine, so they turn off the machine and plan to continue later.
